surprises.description: CTS raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $2.78–$2.88, with the new floor above the preview’s expected $2.72–$2.80+ raise and the new ceiling slightly above its $2.75–$2.85 bull case. The raised floor is the clearest upside relative to the preview’s emphasis on whether guidance would move above $2.70.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to… adjusted diluted EPS of $2.78–$2.88.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $2.72–2.80+ confirms the margin story is structural”; the bull case expected FY guidance of “$2.75–2.85.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 42.2%, well above the preview’s estimated 40.5–41.0% and the 41.5% Q2 record it identified as the key level to watch. The size of the margin gain was stronger than the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached a record 42.2%, up 330 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~40.5–41.0%” and asked whether “41.5% hold[s].”

surprises.description: Management said the unusually favorable project mix behind the record margin should normalize in coming quarters. That is a more explicit warning of a pullback than the preview’s hoped-for framing of the record as a possible new baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned of “normalization in coming quarters due to an unusually favorable project mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the record margin would be “framed as a new baseline rather than a peak.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $150 million, about 2.8% above the $145.96 million consensus and at the top of the preview’s bull-case revenue range. The result beat the central expectation, though it was not above the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 revenue consensus was “$145.96M”; the bull case was “$150–153M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.77 exceeded the $0.653 consensus and the preview’s $0.70–$0.74 buy-side anchor, but about $0.04 came from favorable foreign exchange. Excluding that benefit, the result was roughly $0.73, near the top of the preview’s buy-side range rather than a similarly large underlying beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS hit a record $0.77… including approximately $0.04 of foreign currency favorability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 adjusted EPS consensus was “$0.653”; the preview said buy-side holders were “anchored closer to $0.70–0.74.”

surprises.description: CTS raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $580–$590 million from $565–$585 million. Both ends moved up, although the ranges overlap and the preview did not give a specific expected revised revenue range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $580M-$590M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed existing FY2026 revenue guidance of “$565–585M.”

surprises.description: Transportation revenue grew 2% year-over-year, better than the preview’s base-case expectation of a 2%–5% decline and a reversal from the recent negative trend. The preview had identified a return to growth as an important test for the new CEO.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “transportation -2% to -5%”; the preview also highlighted whether transportation had “returned to growth.”

surprises.description: Diversified end-market revenue grew 7%, below the preview’s expected 12%–15% and below its stated 10% level for preserving the diversification thesis. The result suggests weaker conversion into sales than the preview anticipated, even as the overall quarter beat revenue consensus.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Diversified +12–15%” and said “deceleration below ~+10% breaks the central bull thesis.”

surprises.description: Aerospace and defense bookings were particularly strong at 1.91 book-to-bill, well above the previously reported 1.23 and a strong signal relative to the preview’s expectation that A&D would strengthen. That booking strength had not yet translated into year-over-year sales growth: A&D sales were down 7%, despite rising 30% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace/defense [book-to-bill was] at 1.91”; A&D sales were “down 7% year-over-year but up 30% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited A&D book-to-bill of “1.23” and said A&D would “strengthen in the second half, supported by bookings, backlog and funding deployment.”

surprises.description: Medical bookings weakened sharply: book-to-bill was 0.66, versus the previously reported 1.21, and medical revenue also fell 4% sequentially. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation that medical volumes would normalize and that bookings would convert, although revenue was still up 21% year-over-year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medical lagged at 0.66 due to order timing”; medical revenue “grew 21% year-over-year to $27 million but declined 4% sequentially on order timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited medical book-to-bill of “1.21” and said medical therapeutic volumes would “normalize”; it also expected A&D and medical backlog to ship.

surprises.description: Millar is expected to add about $30 million in annual revenue, above the preview’s estimate of roughly $13–$20 million annualized. CTS also disclosed that the deal is expected to become EPS-accretive in the second half of 2027, a timing detail the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: CTS acquired Millar for “approximately $50 million in cash,” expected to add “~$30 million in annual revenue” and become “EPS accretive in the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Millar’s contribution at “~$13–20M annualized” and said revenue contribution was not disclosed.
